text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Turkey's Islamist minister of justice has threathened prosecutors and judges who attend an army briefing on Islamic fundemantalism with posting to distant provinces.
- A Turkish family of four has to pay at least 200 million lira ($1,400) for a first class week-long holiday in Turkey.
MILLIYET
- The minister of finance said the army will be given extra money to pay for their operation in northern Iraq in August or September.
- The far-right Grand Unity Party (BBP) says it has agreement not to join the Islamist-led coalition government.
HURRIYET
- The conservative wing of the government coalition denies coming last in a public opinion poll and says it is the leading party holding 28 percent of the vote.
- Customs officers are gearing up to fight money laundering after two Islamists firms were caught with illegally imported gold and foriegn currency.
YENI YUZYIL
- A conversation between the military chief and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan reveals the disagreements about the cross-border operation into northern Iraq.
RADIKAL
- The main opposition party is preparing to submit a censure motion over the government's their relations with the military.
- Ninety-five percent of Turkish society is in poverty, while 5 percent of people have got richer over past seven years.
DUNYA
- The ministry of agriculture said that tax imposed on milk and fodder will be decreased to 1 percent.
ZAMAN
- Islamists are mobilising deputies to agree on the changing the law governing Turkish political parties.
CUMHURIYET
- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal says the left is growing in confidence.
